summary: Kisangani, capital of Tshopo province, is a government-held city with no armed group controlling territory. The Congolese National Police (PNC) keep day-to-day order in all communes and neighbourhoods, while the FARDC maintain a large garrison and use Bangboka airport as a strategic logistics and air hub for eastern operations (it was reportedly targeted by long-range drones in 2025, without any change in ground control). Peri-urban and left-bank (Lubunga) villages are assessed under default state presence; Lubunga saw Mbole-Lengola intercommunal clashes in 2023 but no lasting armed-group control. Web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for the city and low elsewhere.

zones.description: Kisangani city: urban settlement records of Kisangani and Lubunga and all health-area neighbourhoods of the communes Makiso, Tshopo, Mangobo, Kabondo, Kisangani and Lubunga (Tshopo and Lubunga health zones)
zones.evidence: Provincial capital of Tshopo, firmly under government authority and far from the M23/ADF frontlines; the PNC runs commissariats and handles arrests and public order, while FARDC (3rd defence zone / regional HQ, Camp Ketele, air assets at Bangboka) are garrisoned in the city. Insecurity is urban crime and occasional unrest, and reported long-range drone strikes on the Bangboka airport area (2025) did not change ground control. zones.description: Bangboka airport area (Bangboka Aeroport locality, Mandombe health area east of the city)
zones.evidence: Bangboka international airport is a key FARDC/air-force logistics hub for operations in the east (aircraft and drone deployments) and is under military guard; the adjoining locality is assessed as army-secured. Neighbouring civilian villages are left with the PNC zone. No web sources could be retrieved in this run (search budget exhausted, search engines blocked).

zones.evidence: Villages on the roads leading out of Kisangani (Buta, Bafwasende, Yangambi axes) inside the city-province's administrative limits with no reported armed-group activity; state police and administration from the city communes cover them. zones.description: Left-bank villages of Lubunga commune and Ubundu road (Yalikutu, Batiamendje, Babula, Yasendo, Ilongo, Babugana, Banango, Pumuzika, Batiagai, Batikatchende, Balasa, Masengo, Babongie, Lowange, Isange, Batikedoki, Batikobabo, Batipanga)
zones.evidence: Rural villages south/west of the Congo River in Lubunga commune toward Ubundu. The area saw Mbole-Lengola intercommunal violence in 2023, answered by police and army deployments, but no armed group is known to hold territory there; state forces are assumed to keep order.
